blocks.html: Chapter 6 built the machinery that describes how a statistic varies from sample to sample: the sampling distribution, the Central Limit Theorem and the standard error. This chapter puts it to work on the one sample you actually have. It covers the single best guess (point estimation, §7.1), the range of plausible values around it (confidence intervals, §7.2), how large a sample must be for a chosen precision (§7.3), and the rates, standardised rates and life tables through which Indian health statistics are reported (§7.4–7.5).
